newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's parliament approves 1997 balanced budget.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's parliament approves 1997 balanced budget.

text.p: Turkey's parliament on Wednesday approved the Islamist-led government's ambitious zero-deficit budget for 1997, the parliamentary speaker announced.
Speaker Mustafa Kalemli said 279 deputies voted in favour of the budget draft and 243 against. One vote was invalid.

"This budget, for the first time in fifty years, is a balanced budget. Passing such a budget is an honour for this parliament," Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan said in a speech immediately after the result was announced.

The government's draft budget programmes basic revenues of 5,095 trillion Turkish lira ($48 billion) and "other revenues" amounting to 1,161 trillion ($11 billion), compared with spending of 6,256 trillion lira ($59 billion).
Turkish bankers and businessmen have said they are highly sceptical about the budgetary targets.

The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has also expressed concern over the targets and forecast a rise in Turkey's budget deficit in 1997. Turkey's budget deficit in 1996 is expected to reach 1,300 trillion lira ($12 billion).

Turkey's privatisation agency OIB targets revenues of some $5 billion from sell-offs in 1997, but the IMF has said privatisation revenues programmed in the draft budget were unlikely to reach state coffers until 1998.

The government's aim of raising a further 300 trillion lira ($2.8 billion) from the sale of state property was dealt a serious blow last week when the constitutional court annulled the law that enabled the sales to take place. ($=105,530)
